results.evidence: Fifth pass (r14, 2026-10-01), web only, Internet Archive full-text search as the new angle; still one spot-specific author (the land manager); no ops. NEW: (1) The crag guidebook (Weekend Rock Washington, 2005 scan) IS reachable through Internet Archive full-text search snippets even though the scan is lend-only. Its Half Moon Crags beta block reads, in walked snippets: Getting there: Drive US 2 to Stevens Pass. Half Moon Group: From a junction just 100 yards west of the summit sign, locate the old Stevens Pass Highway, which takes off in a northwesterly direction down the drainage. In about 1.4 miles ... The same book states pass rules where they apply (introduction: some areas require a Northwest Forest Pass, although a good number are still free; Washington Pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at the Blue Lake trailhead), but no snippet from the Half Moon pages mentions a pass, fee or permit either way. Snippets are fragments, so this is an absence in what could be read, not a statement; not counted. (2) Wild Roads Washington (2012), drive 36 Old Cascade Highway: Stevens Pass to Wellington: its pass NOTES found say a Northwest Forest Pass is not required at the Iron Goat Wayside and is required at the Wellington and Martin Creek trailheads (the listed fee sites); nothing about the hairpin pull-off. Consistent with the land manager, but it does not speak to this spot. (3) Google Books snippet API quota is still exhausted; the legacy books feed answered but returned nothing for this crag. Net: unchanged, one author. Owner note unchanged: the row contradicts itself (access.notes not a developed fee site, access.parking_pass no fee site identified, passRequired Recreation pass); if accepted, the op is passRequired "Recreation pass" -> a no-pass value on these five rows only; access.fees and access._raw untouched.

results.resolution: Day 1 (Tupso Pass trailhead to Goat Flats) is 4.5 mi one way, stated by two independent guidebooks (and a third hiking site); 7.3 is replaced with 4.5 in days[0].miles and the totalNote.
results.summary: Two guidebooks both put Goat Flats 4.5 miles from the Tupso Pass trailhead, so day 1 now reads 4.5 mi instead of 7.3.
results.evidence: Internet Archive full-text search (new angle). (A) 75 Scrambles in Washington (Mountaineers Books, 2001), Three Fingers waypoint list: "1. trailhead: 3100 ft (10U 591405mE 5338345mN) 2. Saddle Lake: 2.5 miles, 3780 ft ... 3. Goat Flat: 4.5 miles, 5000 ft ... 4. Tin Can Gap: 6 miles, 5700 ft"; its drive is FR 41 to Tupso Pass, right onto FS Road 4160, trailhead at 17.3 miles - the same old Tupso Pass trailhead the row uses (identified by its description: the FS 4160 road end past Tupso Pass; the book’s UTM converts to about 0.7 km from the row trailhead pin, likely a datum/era difference, and is not used for any pin). (B) Exploring Washington’s Wild Areas (Mountaineers Books, 2002), Boulder River Wilderness: "The path starts from near the end of FR 41 at Tupso Pass ... [a spur] leads to Saddle Lake; the main trail continues to Goat Flat, 4.5 miles from the trailhead." Different authors and books, both stating 4.5 mi one way from the same trailhead; a third, the WTA Goat Flats page, also says 4.5 (already logged in r8). The row itself already says Goat Flats ~4.5 mi total in approach and approach_variants. Not used: Day Hiking North Cascades (segment wording), Moon/Washington Handbook (2.3/2.5 mi beyond Saddle Lake, segments), Pacific Northwest Hiking (12.4 mi round trip to the lookout). Day 1 hours (4.5), gain and the 2-day structure are left as they are. OWNER FOLLOW-UP, not written: day 2 (miles 7.7, note "hike the full ~7.5 miles back out") is now inconsistent with a 4.5 mi day 1; no source states a day-2 figure (it would have to be computed), so it is left for the owner. Third op added by the session owner: day 2 note restates the same sourced 4.5-mile trailhead-Goat Flat segment for the walk out (not a computed figure), so the tab does not say 4.5 in and 7.5 out. Day 2 miles (7.7) left as is.

results.resolution: Only one source states a Foggy Dew trailhead -> Cooney Lake figure on the row’s Merchants Basin line (8.5 mi); no second agrees.
results.summary: One mountain-bike guide puts Cooney Lake 8.5 miles up the Foggy Dew / Merchants Basin line; no second source states that figure, so day 1 (6.2) is left alone.
results.evidence: Internet Archive full-text search plus the legacy Google Books feed (new angles). ON THE ROW’S LINE: Mountain Bike America: Washington (1998), ride Foggy Dew Creek/Merchants Basin, mileage log: "0.0 START riding up the Foggy Dew Creek Trail #417 ... 7.6 Reach the top of Merchants Basin and the trail junction ... over the pass toward Cooney Lake. 8.5 Arrive at the Cooney Lake Campsite ... 16.5 Arrive back at the Foggy Dew Creek Trailhead parking area." A stated cumulative one-way figure, single source. NOT the row’s line, so not counted: Backpacking Washington (Romano, 2011) trip planner 7.7 / 8 miles - Martin Creek line, same author as the Hike of the Week figure already logged; 100 Hikes in the North Cascades (Spring, 1988/1994/2000) Cooney Lake, round trip 16 via Martin Creek trail No. 429, no one-way figure; Best Hikes with Dogs (Nelson) "about 8.5 miles from the trailhead" - its trailhead is the Eagle Lakes / Crater Creek one (the text crosses Eagle Creek and climbs the end of the Martin Creek valley), a different start; Beckey Rainy Pass to Fraser River and 100 Hikes give only segments (Merchants Basin at 6 mi, Cooney Lake 3.3 mi from a junction); Day Hiking North Cascades (Romano) loop segments; Mountain Bike Adventures (Kirkendall) loop log starts elsewhere. Google Books API quota still exhausted. Owner note: the only stated figure on this line (8.5) and the row’s own Cooney Lake pin (distMi 8) both contradict 6.2, which also appears in days[1].note and underlies day 2’s 12.8; a fix still needs a second source.
